title: GitHub - sao-coding/locus: A fast, smooth database client for Windows. Built with Rust and GPUI.
excerpt: A fast, smooth database client for Windows. Built with Rust and GPUI. - sao-coding/locus
content_html:
English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文

A database client for Windows that stays smooth. GPU-rendered, written in Rust, one small exe.

Locus talks to MySQL / MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Redis, Oracle and SQL Server. Results stream into the grid while the query is still running, and cancelling really stops the query on the server.

Why Locus

  • It does not freeze. Big results stream into a virtualized grid. A slow query or a huge table does not block typing, scrolling or switching tabs.
  • It is careful with production. A connection marked Production is read-only by default. Writes need a timed unlock, every writing statement asks for its own confirmation, and each one lands in an audit log. The gate classifies the statement text; functions called by a SELECT are not checked for side effects, except known built-ins (nextval, pg_terminate_backend, GET_LOCK ...).
  • It stays out of your way. One window, vertical tabs, split panes, and a command palette for everything else.

Features

Workspace

  • Spaces: group connections and tabs, each with its own color
  • Vertical tabs; split the work area into up to 4 panes (Ctrl+Shift+M zooms one temporarily)
  • Command palette (Ctrl+K), query history, light / dark / system theme, English, 简体中文 and 繁體中文

Connections

  • MySQL / MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite and Redis connect directly from Rust; Oracle and SQL Server go through a small Go helper (sidecar.exe, built into locus.exe)
  • SSH tunnels; passwords are stored in the Windows Credential Manager
  • Production protection: read-only by default, timed unlock, audit log

Query

  • SQL editor with syntax highlighting, find / replace, formatting, completion, and JOIN suggestions taken from foreign keys
  • Query parameters, saved queries and snippets
  • Auto-commit or manual transactions with Commit / Rollback
  • Execution plans

Results

  • Streaming grid, server-side cancel, filters, selection statistics
  • Follow a foreign key to the referenced row
  • Edit cells in place; changes are applied inside a transaction
  • Value viewer: text, JSON tree, hex, image

Objects

  • Object tree with paging and server-side search
  • Table structure tab, relationship diagram
  • Source and compile for stored procedures, functions, triggers and Oracle packages

Import and export

  • Import CSV and Excel
  • Export CSV, xlsx, JSON, SQL INSERT, Markdown and HTML, including streaming the full result from the server

Administration

  • Server activity: sessions, kill a query, server variables
  • Redis: key browser, a viewer for each value type, command window

Performance

Loading a 1,000,000-row, 12-column table with SELECT *, Locus on the left, DBeaver 26.0.5 on the right. Locus shows rows while they are still arriving and lets you stop the query; the GIF is real time.

Locus DBeaver
Load time, 1,000,000 rows 1.5 to 1.7 s (3 runs) 2.9 s (1 run; a second run failed with a driver error)
Memory when idle about 100 MB about 340 MB
Memory right after the load about 360 MB about 1.3 GB (peak 1.4 GB)
Memory after closing the result about 107 MB, within seconds about 1.37 GB, not released

How it was measured: Intel Core i5-14400F, 15.8 GB RAM, Windows 11, MariaDB 11.8.5 on the same machine over 127.0.0.1, no TLS. Locus is the release build with the per-tab row limit off (a separate 1,000,000-row memory cap, set in Settings, still applies; this table has exactly that many rows). DBeaver uses its default 1 GB heap with the fetch size raised to 1,000,000 (its default is 200), so it loads everything at once. Memory is the process's private memory sampled about once a second. The two programs were measured in separate sessions, and DBeaver only once, so read the DBeaver column as one observation, not a benchmark. Locus is not always faster: on a 100,000-row result both were done in under a second.

Install

Download from Releases and either run the installer locus-<version>-windows-x64-setup.exe (per user, no admin, with a Start menu entry and an uninstaller) or run the portable locus-<version>-windows-x64.exe, one file with nothing to install. Oracle and SQL Server support is built in, no extra file needed: the first Oracle or SQL Server connection unpacks a small helper into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Locus\sidecar\.

The builds are not code-signed, so SmartScreen may warn the first time. To check a download:

# compare with the .sha256 file on the release page
Get-FileHash .\locus-<version>-windows-x64.exe -Algorithm SHA256

# build provenance, with the GitHub CLI
gh attestation verify .\locus-<version>-windows-x64.exe --repo sao-coding/locus

# minisign signature (the key is also in minisign.pub)
minisign -Vm .\locus-<version>-windows-x64.exe -P RWRDNREpYa8EZ59rUGsAnTVNIMjNfUWhciyq6SgS2MpNZvMGj0yVAZ0s

Settings, saved connections and history live in %APPDATA%\Locus. Delete the folder to reset. The Oracle helper is the only file outside it (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Locus\sidecar\); delete that folder too to remove everything.

About once a day Locus asks GitHub whether a newer release exists (only User-Agent: Locus/<version> is sent) and shows it in the status bar. A new version is downloaded in the background and installed only when you pick Restart and update; it is installed only if its minisign signature is from the key in minisign.pub. A Scoop install is left to scoop update. Both are switched in Settings › About.

Keyboard

Keys Action
Ctrl+K / Ctrl+Shift+P Command palette
Ctrl+Enter / Ctrl+Shift+Enter Run the statement at the cursor / the whole script
Ctrl+E Explain the statement at the cursor
Ctrl+S Save query
Ctrl+T / Ctrl+W New tab / close tab
Ctrl+\ / Ctrl+Shift+\ Split right / split down
Ctrl+Shift+M Zoom the current pane
Ctrl+1…9 Switch Space
Ctrl+B / Ctrl+J Sidebar / right panel
Ctrl+Shift+E Export the result
Ctrl+, Settings

Settings has the full list.

FAQ

Which Windows versions work? Windows 10 and 11, 64-bit.

Which databases? MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Redis, Oracle and SQL Server. There is no ClickHouse or MongoDB support.

Does Oracle need an Oracle client? No. The helper uses a pure-Go driver (go-ora), and is built into locus.exe, so there is nothing to install. It is unpacked to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Locus\sidecar\ on the first Oracle connection.

Is my password sent anywhere? No. See Privacy.

Reporting a problem

Open an issue. Say which database and version you connect to, and what you did. Never paste passwords or connection strings. For a security problem, see SECURITY.md and do not open a public issue.

Building from source

You need Windows, a recent stable Rust, and Go (for the Oracle helper).

cargo build --release -p app       # target\release\locus.exe
.\sidecar\build.ps1                # sidecar\bin\sidecar.exe
cargo test --workspace --lib --bins

Do not regenerate Cargo.lock: gpui-kit is a snapshot and a fresh resolve breaks the build. More in CONTRIBUTING.md. A map of the source is in docs/README.md.

Privacy

Locus has no telemetry, no account, no update check and no network traffic of its own. It only connects to the databases and SSH hosts you configure. Passwords go to the Windows Credential Manager, never to a file. Query history and audit logs stay in %APPDATA%\Locus on your machine, and result data is never written there. The only other file Locus writes is the Oracle helper in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Locus\sidecar\.

Acknowledgements

  • GPUI and gpui-kit for the UI
  • Arc for the idea behind Spaces and vertical tabs

The licenses of all bundled components are in THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md.

License
